criteria.criterion: athena.toml contains a [landing] table with merge_via_rest = true, preceded by a comment giving the reason (owner set the repo squash-only with a ruleset on main and approved merging verified work once required checks pass). No other setting changes.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: athena.toml only gains, at the end, `[landing]`, a three-line comment and `merge_via_rest = true`. The comment says the owner set the repository to squash-only merges, put a ruleset on main that requires checks, and approved merging verified work once those checks pass. No other line in the file changes.

criteria.criterion: The test no longer asserts REPO_CONFIG lacks [landing]; it builds a config with the [landing] table removed (not by appending a second table, which would be a duplicate) and asserts the default is off.
criteria.evidence: In config.rs the line `assert!(!REPO_CONFIG.contains("[landing]"))` is removed. The new test builds `base` by walking REPO_CONFIG line by line and dropping everything from the `[landing]` header up to the next header. It then asserts `!base.contains("[landing]")` and that `Config::parse(&base)` gives merge_via_rest false.

criteria.criterion: The test asserts Config::parse(REPO_CONFIG) has landing.merge_via_rest true, and still checks that an explicit true and an empty [landing] table behave as before, using a stripped base.
criteria.evidence: The test asserts `Config::parse(REPO_CONFIG).unwrap().landing.merge_via_rest`. The `on` config (`{base}` plus `[landing] merge_via_rest = true`) is asserted true, and the `empty` config (`{base}` plus a bare `[landing]`) is asserted false. Both are built from the stripped base.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`; all tests pass, including config::tests::rest_merge_is_off_unless_the_config_turns_it_on.
criteria.evidence: `cargo test --locked` finished without an error. Its full output was too large to show and I could not search the saved copy, so the per-suite totals come from Athena's own run (376 tests passed). The targeted run printed `test config::tests::rest_merge_is_off_unless_the_config_turns_it_on ... ok` and `1 passed; 0 failed`.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --locked` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean.
criteria.evidence: Clippy finished every crate with no warnings. `cargo fmt --check` printed nothing and exited with status 0.

The diff also changes CHANGELOG.md (4 lines added under Unreleased/Added). The request says "Only athena.toml and that test change". The brief's expected deliverables do list CHANGELOG.md, which contradicts this criterion. I found no repository rule that requires a changelog entry for every change: a search of README.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/enforcement.md found none.

findings.summary: CHANGELOG.md is changed, but the request and criterion 6 allow only athena.toml and the test to change.
findings.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1` adds a four-line Unreleased/Added entry to CHANGELOG.md. The user wrote "Only athena.toml and that test change." The brief's own deliverables list includes CHANGELOG.md, so the brief contradicts itself. Either the entry is dropped, or the user confirms that it is wanted.

findings.summary: The changelog entry sits under 'Added', but it describes a configuration change and a test fix.
findings.evidence: Under Keep a Changelog, a setting change and a test fix fit 'Changed' better than 'Added'.

summary: The core change is correct, but the verdict is fail on one point: the candidate also edits CHANGELOG.md. athena.toml now has a `[landing]` table with `merge_via_rest = true` and a comment giving the reason, and nothing else in the file changes. The test now strips the `[landing]` table from the repository's config to check that the default is off, checks that an explicit true and an empty table still behave as before, and asserts that this repository's config turns the merge on. That fixes the root cause the user named: the test pinned the live setting instead of the default. `cargo test --locked`, the targeted test, `cargo clippy --locked` and `cargo fmt --check` all passed when I ran them. The request said "Only athena.toml and that test change" and criterion 6 repeats it, but the candidate also adds a CHANGELOG.md entry. The brief's own deliverables list includes CHANGELOG.md, so the brief contradicts itself on this. To pass, either remove the changelog entry or have the user confirm they want it.
